answer: Each identity locks 60 credits in a plume bond. The plume board publishes timestamps and hashes for audit. At each cedar checkpoint, identities sharing timing and outputs are grouped: the k-th member pays 5 credits per earlier member, so its marginal cost is 60 + 5(k-1). A 1,000-clone cluster costs 2,557,500 credits, bonds burned on duplication. An honest agent pays 60 once. A rented farm that jitters timestamps fails: cedar clustering also matches output hashes, so jittered clones stay clustered and each locks its own bond. The nectar pool pays auditors from burned bonds.
